collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The caregivers bring a list of problems the leaders missed: hear them now, or let them fix things themselves.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The people who look after the village's children and sick have held their own meeting, and (subject) has come to the gathering with a list: the children's water is fetched too far, the night fires are too close to the sleeping mats, and the food is shared before the nursing parents can get any. (friend) says the gathering has other business. What should the gathering do?

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The gathering hears the whole list. Most of it is fixed within the week. The night fires are moved. The food is shared later. (friend) admits (friend.he/she) had never noticed any of it.

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The caregivers fix what they can themselves: they move the fires, change the food sharing, dig a new water path. It is hard work, and they are tired, and a little bitter that nobody else helped.
